title: Gore-Tex and Performance Membranes
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: Gore-Tex, ePTFE membranes, and technical textiles.
final_note: Pores too small for liquid water, big enough for water vapour.

concepts.def: ePTFE membrane laminate, invented by Bob Gore in 1969.
Transmits water vapour while resisting liquid water.
Bonding a membrane between fabric layers.
DuPont elastane fibre (1958), highly elastic spandex.
Textile engineered for performance rather than aesthetics.

walkthroughs.body_html: Bob Gore stretched PTFE in 1969 and discovered the resulting ePTFE membrane was strong, micro-porous and waterproof. Marketed as Gore-Tex from 1976, it transformed outdoor clothing.

Gore-Tex membrane has ~9 billion pores per square inch. Each pore is ~20,000 times smaller than a water droplet but ~700 times larger than a water vapour molecule — keeping rain out, letting sweat escape.
Lycra (elastane/spandex) was invented by Joseph Shivers at DuPont in 1958. A few % Lycra in a blend gives stretch and recovery — transforming sportswear, swimwear and tailoring.
